tasks.short: Help travellers prepare required travel documents and forms.

steps.what: Clarify the journey and collect traveller details.
Check official requirements for the traveller and itinerary.
Inspect supplied documents and identify missing or inconsistent details.

loop.input: Traveller documents and the required field schema.
loop.output: Extracted fields, source locations and unreadable-field flags.
loop.check: Validate formats and cross-document consistency; show source snippets for human verification. Do not infer authenticity.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry per document; unreadable or conflicting fields go to the reservation agent.
loop.why_not_simpler: Scans and document layouts vary; fixed field mapping cannot reliably read all supplied documents.

steps.what: Copy verified details into the required travel forms.
Explain missing items and resolve questions about completing the forms.
Review the completed forms with the traveller and obtain required signatures.

tasks.design: A guided form in the {WORKFLOW} collects traveller details once, while a dated requirements table in the {DOCS} produces a checklist for agent review. A bounded extraction loop reads supplied documents; deterministic mappings generate forms in the {DOCS} after field verification. The traveller approves declarations and signatures, with submission kept separate from preparation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document formats vary, official requirements change, and forms often require repeated entry across disconnected channels.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and document tools cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the cost of field mappings and validation, while bounded extraction handles varied scans.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping requirements current, interpreting unusual circumstances and supporting official forms without stable interfaces remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Explain uncertain requirements calmly, notice inconsistencies and recognise when the traveller needs an official authority or specialist.

ambition.what: A pre-departure document readiness review with a personalised missing-item list.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying details to resolving document exceptions and offering readiness reviews. The agent gains no authority to determine entry eligibility or sign traveller declarations.

reach.learn: Plain-language correspondence, approved wording and secure document handling.

evidence.claim: Document extraction with validation and exception routing exists for order documents; travel-document performance needs separate testing.
Verified fields can populate fixed forms through deterministic mappings.
GDPR requires a lawful basis, limited collection and appropriate protection for traveller documents.

assumptions: A mid-size travel business handles recurring document and form types.
The agent assists with preparation; official authorities determine entry eligibility.
Build estimates cover an initial set of forms and destinations, not worldwide coverage.
The means mix includes substantial face-to-face explanation and document inspection, consistent with the supplied priors.
unknowns: Which forms, destinations and traveller categories dominate actual demand.
Whether official requirements can be accessed and reused reliably.
Which systems permit field-level access and document storage.
Accepted signature methods and the business's permitted advisory scope.
Retention periods, lawful bases and applicable national rules for employee consultation.
research_questions: Which required fields can be mapped without interpreting legal eligibility?
How often do document layouts or official requirements change?
What extraction errors appear in representative scans and languages?
new_work: Verify extracted identity fields against their source documents.
Maintain requirements, source dates and form mappings.
Handle unreadable documents and ambiguous requirements.
Maintain access controls, deletion schedules and integration checks.
Complete employee consultation under national rules where applicable.

tasks.short: Help passengers who need assistance board or leave transport safely.

steps.what: Read the assistance request in the reservation system {OTHER}.
Meet the passenger and confirm their preferred assistance.
Assess the route, equipment and conditions before moving.
Coordinate the boarding or disembarking handover with transport staff.
Assist the passenger physically and complete the agreed handover.
Record completion and exceptions in the reservation system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure the reservation system {OTHER} to pass minimum necessary assistance details into a mobile queue in the {WORKFLOW}. Staff acknowledge handovers and confirm prefilled completion records, while missed acknowledgements trigger notifications. Passenger conversations, route checks and physical assistance remain with trained people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assistance details, departure changes and staff handovers sit in separate operational channels. Much of the task requires physical presence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing queues, forms and notifications can remove repeated coordination where interfaces are available. AI-assisted coding can make a small connector cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Live conditions, equipment availability, passenger comfort and reliable handovers require trained staff and local knowledge.
tasks.human_edge: Respect the passenger's autonomy, adapt assistance in the moment and recognise unsafe conditions.
tasks.altitude: Most of the week and all safety decision rights stay the same. Staff spend slightly less time locating requests and recording completed assistance.

reach.task: Coordinate recovery when assistance handovers are missed.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, escalation thresholds and transport-provider responsibilities.

evidence.claim: Structured requests, acknowledgements and completion records can use deterministic workflow automation.
Software coordination does not replace physical assistance or on-site safety judgement.
Assistance records may reveal health information and require appropriate GDPR safeguards and processing conditions.

assumptions: This task occurs at staffed transport locations rather than a booking-only office.
Staff have required training and equipment.
The future uses operational acknowledgements rather than employee performance scoring.
The decomposition keeps 85% of today's time in person, close to the supplied means prior.
unknowns: Which reservation interfaces and existing assistance queues are available.
Who employs assistance workers and owns each handover.
Whether staff can use mobile devices throughout the location.
Which assistance details need retention and who may access them.
Applicable national rules for employee consultation and operational changes.
research_questions: Can the existing system already configure request routing and acknowledgements?
Where do missed handovers actually occur?
What must the workflow do during connectivity loss or departure changes?
new_work: Handle unacknowledged requests and stale departure information.
Maintain routing rules, staff access and fallback procedures.
Review exception records without collecting unnecessary medical detail.
Check that workflow use does not distract staff during physical assistance.
Complete employee consultation under national rules where applicable.

tasks.short: Suggest travel options and provide useful guides, maps and information sources.

steps.what: Ask about the traveller's destination, timing, interests and practical constraints.
Find relevant guides, maps and current information in the {DOCS} and {CMS}.
Compare suitable options against the traveller's preferences.
Assemble selected suggestions, guides and maps for the traveller.
Explain the suggestions and answer the traveller's follow-up questions.
Send the selected information and links to the traveller.

tasks.design: Index approved resources from the {DOCS} and {CMS} in the {HELPDESK}, using destination tags, update dates and practical constraints. Deterministic filters prepare options for agent review, then an artefact generator assembles a personalised travel pack with source links and dates. The {WORKFLOW} sends the selected pack through the {EMAIL} after the conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful information is scattered across guides and pages, with inconsistent tags and update dates. Agents repeatedly gather and assemble similar material.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing knowledge search, forms and templates cover the main steps. AI-assisted coding can reduce the cost of connecting them and building preference filters.
tasks.still_hard: Resource freshness, subjective preferences and reliable accessibility information need continuing attention. Dynamic availability needs a current source.
tasks.human_edge: Understand unstated preferences and explain practical trade-offs, especially when published information is incomplete.

ambition.what: A personalised mobile travel pack combining suggestions, maps and dated source links.

tasks.altitude: The agent spends less time searching and assembling material and more time discussing suitable options. They can select and order approved resources; pricing, booking and policy rights do not change.

reach.task: Maintain shared destination directions and visitor information.
reach.learn: Source verification, accessible information design and resource tagging.

evidence.claim: Knowledge-base answering with handover to a prefilled request is available today.
Tagged resources, deterministic filters and templates can assemble travel information without a model loop.
Support-assistant research found productivity gains, but does not establish a travel-information-specific saving.

assumptions: The business has a manageable set of approved destinations and information sources.
Resources can be tagged and reused lawfully.
Routine preference capture can use a short form, with conversation available.
This decomposition assigns more time to resource retrieval and assembly than the in-person prior; local observation should test that choice.
The initial design uses no conversational AI and needs no autonomous agent.
unknowns: Which sources staff currently trust and may redistribute.
Whether maps and guides support accessible mobile formats.
How often customers need live fares, availability or disruption information.
Actual demand by language and destination.
Who maintains resources and approves recommendation criteria.
Applicable access requirements and national employee consultation rules.
research_questions: Can existing knowledge search meet retrieval needs after better tagging?
Which questions require judgement rather than a resource lookup?
Which source fields need expiry dates or live checks?
Can travellers use the resulting pack on their own devices?
new_work: Maintain resource tags, source dates and broken-link checks.
Review filtered suggestions against traveller constraints.
Maintain pack templates and accessible formats.
Handle unusual requests and questions outside the approved resource set.

role.altitude: The role shifts towards document exceptions and useful travel conversations, while physical passenger assistance changes little. Administrative preparation becomes faster; legal eligibility and transport safety authority remain with the responsible people.
reach: Correspondence clerk: prepare clear document requests using approved wording.
Information clerk: maintain reliable destination resources and directions.
Office support supervisor: coordinate recovery from missed assistance handovers.
skills_to_grow: Verify extracted fields against source documents.
Maintain dated requirements and information sources.
Recognise exceptions that need an official authority or specialist.
Use accessible communication and respect passenger preferences.
Handle workflow failures and protect traveller information.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a joined pre-departure readiness service that combines document preparation and personalised travel packs, with trained staff handling sensitive questions and physical assistance.

job.title: Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks
